source: MACE docs, Fine-tuning Foundation Models, 'Naive Fine-tuning' command (https://mace-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide/finetuning.html): --foundation_model, --multiheads_finetuning=False, --energy_weight=10.0, --forces_weight=10.0, --E0s=estimated, --lr=0.001, --weight_decay=0.0, --scaling=rms_forces_scaling, --batch_size=2, --max_num_epochs=6, --ema, --ema_decay=0.999, --amsgrad, --clip_grad=1.0, --default_dtype=float64. Values below are that command's, unchanged. No hyperparameter search; the validation split is used only for the tool's own checkpoint selection (lowest validation loss).
why_naive_not_multihead: The pre-registration says 'each tool's documented fine-tuning defaults for a small dataset'. The documented small-dataset command is the naive one. Multihead replay (the library default, --multiheads_finetuning=True) additionally needs the MPtrj replay set (--pt_train_file=mp, a download) and a two-head model whose calculator needs head selection; it is a different method from the one documented for small data.

added_to_the_documented_command.valid_file/train_file: explicit 90/10 split files (the doc uses --valid_fraction=0.05 --test_file); the held-out sets are never given to mace_run_train
added_to_the_documented_command.foundation_model_elements_why: keeps all 89 elements of MACE-MP-0 in the fine-tuned model; without it the model holds only the 8 training elements and the S2 forgetting control (Si, Mg, Na, Cl, Cu, C, Ce, O) cannot be run at all

foundation_model_is: mace_mp(model='medium'), the checkpoint of the paper (mlip_dynstab.calculators._mace_mp0 default)
epoch_budget_deviation: 2026-10-03, before any training data: budget raised from the documented 6 to 30 epochs (pre-registration Deviations D2). The documented value targets a different dataset size; at ~54 optimiser steps per epoch it would leave a refuted P1 indistinguishable from under-training. Selection stays on the validation split only (lowest validation loss); every other setting is the documented one.
